items.title: Week 6 — Conjecturing with interior and closure
items.statement: Work with Topology Peer to investigate how interior and closure interact with unions and intersections. Formulate plausible identities involving $\operatorname{int}(A\cup B)$, $\operatorname{int}(A\cap B)$, $\overline{A\cup B}$, and $\overline{A\cap B}$. Test your conjectures on examples. When a conjecture fails, find a counterexample and see whether it can be replaced by a weaker statement that is always true. When you believe a statement is true, try to prove it.
items.initial_prompt: Begin by inviting the student to make one plausible conjecture involving interior or closure and a union or intersection. Act as a conjecture-testing partner: test examples, seek counterexamples when appropriate, repair false statements, and then prove surviving statements. Do not list the standard identities at the outset.
items.tutor_instructions: Once a conjecture has been resolved, give the student the first opportunity to propose the next conjecture or comparison rather than automatically moving through a predetermined list of interior/closure identities. Keep the exploration adaptive while still helping the student encounter a useful mix of true identities, false identities, counterexamples, and repaired inclusions.
